subject: Recap: Dedicated capacity discovery — forecasted TPS & burst policy
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Amy Jenkins <amy.jenkins@averyretail.com>, Ben Torres <ben.torres@averyretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-15T16:05:00-08:00
Subject: Recap: Dedicated capacity discovery — forecasted TPS & burst policy

Hi Amy / Ben —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap of what we heard, the success criteria you outlined, and suggested next steps so we stay aligned. I kept this tight — please flag anything I missed.

Key pain points you described
- Unpredictable token costs and latency spikes during promotions (Black Friday windows)
- Strict data isolation requirement for PII-sensitive recommendation requests
- Current infra (on-prem + managed GPU instances) lacks automated burst capacity and warms slowly for cold starts

Current stack details you shared
- Serving: in-house microservice calling an open-weights transformer hosted in GCP (NVIDIA A100s)
- Frontend qps: baseline ~120 TPS; expected seasonal peaks up to ~850 TPS for short bursts (5–20 min)
- Authentication & data flow: tokens contain customer IDs; PII stripped upstream but audit logs must be retained for 90 days

Success criteria (your priorities)
1) Latency p95 <= 250ms at baseline and <= 450ms during allowed burst periods
2) Predictable monthly inference cost within a 10% tolerance vs committed spend
3) VPC-isolated control plane and customer-managed KMS for keys
4) Autoscaling that can support 4–8x short-lived burst capacity without impacting baseline SLOs

Redwood Dedicated fit notes
- Reserved GPU pools map cleanly to predictability requirement; we can size pools to cover baseline TPS with headroom for steady-state autoscale.
- Burst policy: propose a two-tier burst model — (A) warm burst nodes reserved but spot-priced for predictable short bursts, (B) overflow on shared capacity with automated throttles and fallbacks to a smaller model if latency targets are threatened.
- Isolation & compliance: Dedicated supports private control plane + VPC peering and customer KMS; we can provide audit logs with 90d retention per your requirement.

Open technical questions (please confirm)
- Can you share the distribution of request sequence lengths (median / 90th pct)? That affects kernel selection and pool sizing.
- Which endpoints must be pinned to private routing (recommendations vs analytics)?
- Any contractual constraints on preemptible capacity during peak windows?

Proposed next steps
1) Technical follow-up with your infra lead to collect sequence-length histogram + traffic patterns (target: 45-minute call this week)
2) Redwood to deliver an initial sizing + pricing sketch for a dedicated pool with burst policy (ETA: 48 business hours after the infra call)
3) Security questionnaire kickoff (we’ll attach SOC2 evidence and an initial network diagram)

Attachments: a short PDF with the sizing checklist and the one-pager on Dedicated features.

If this looks right I’ll loop in Solutions (Marissa) and our SRE (Sean) to set the infra call.

Thanks —
Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Amy Jenkins <amy.jenkins@averyretail.com>

Date: 2026-11-16T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Recap: Dedicated capacity discovery — forecasted TPS & burst policy

Karthik —

Thanks for the clear recap. Looks accurate. A couple clarifications:
- Sequence lengths: median ~64 tokens, 90th ~410 tokens. We’ll extract a histogram for you (should be ready in the infra call).
- Endpoints to pin: recommendation inference must be private; analytics batch endpoints can remain on public routing.
- Preemptible constraint: we prefer no preemptible during peak promotional windows; outside of those hours short-lived preemptible capacity is acceptable.

We’re available for the infra call Thursday 2026-11-18 at 09:00 PT. Ben and I will bring our infra engineer (Jai) and the security owner (Natalie).

Please send an invite and any prep notes. Appreciate it.

— Amy
VP, Product & Data | Avery Retail
amy.jenkins@averyretail.com | +1 (206) 555-0144

Perfect — thanks Amy. Invite sent for Thu 2026-11-18 09:00 PT with a short agenda. Prep notes attached (what we need from your infra team) and the sizing checklist I mentioned.

Agenda highlights
- Quick traffic histogram review (5–10 min)
- Pool sizing options & burst policy tradeoffs (20 min)
- Security checklist / KMS & network controls (15 min)
- Next steps & timing for pricing sketch (5 min)

I’m copying Marissa (Solutions Eng) and Sean (SRE) so they can lead the technical section. We’ll also bring a short cost model showing committed vs burst economics.

Talk Thursday —
Karthik

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Amy Jenkins <amy.jenkins@averyretail.com>, Ben Torres <ben.torres@averyretail.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-18T10:12:00-08:00
Subject: Follow-up: infra call notes & immediate asks (post-call)

Hi Amy / Ben —

Thanks for the call this morning; appreciate Jai and Natalie joining. Brief notes + immediate asks so we can run the sizing exercise by EOW: 

Notes from the call
- Confirmed traffic histogram: baseline 120 TPS steady-state; median seq 64; 95th seq ~520 tokens; promotional peaks ~800–900 TPS but typically <20 minutes
- Required p95 baseline latency <= 250ms; promotional window p95 <= 450ms
- Data isolation: recommendation requests must traverse private subnet and use customer-managed KMS for at-rest encryption

Immediate asks (action items)
1) Please share the 7-day request histogram export (CSV) to the Drive folder we created: https://drive.redwood.ai/avery/infra-diagram-v2 — file name: avery_7d_histogram.csv
2) Confirm any blackout dates for preemptible/spot capacity (we need specific promo windows for contract language)
3) If you have existing audit log retention policy docs, drop them in the same Drive folder

What we’ll deliver next (target: EOW)
- Two sizing options: (A) conservative reserved pool that covers baseline + 1.5x steady burst; (B) aggressive smaller reserved pool + larger managed overflow with model-fallback policy. Each option will include estimated monthly cost, expected p95 latency, and recommended growth buffer.
- A draft SLA addendum for promotional burst behavior and an appendix for KMS/network setup.

Attachments included: sizing-checklist.xlsx (stub), redwood_dedicated_one-pager.pdf.

Thanks — I’ll ping when the sketch is ready.

Best,
Marissa
Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | +1 (650) 555-0222
